summary.headline: Self-serve with no review: you can have an X OAuth 2.0 app working with Composio in an afternoon. There is no free tier, though. You prepay credits and pay for every call your agent makes for every user ($0.015 per post, $0.20 per post with a link, $0.005 per post read).
summary.overview: You create X OAuth apps in the X Developer Console (console.x.com), and they use OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE. There is no app review, test-user cap or unverified-app warning, so any X user can connect as soon as your app exists. Pay-per-use launched on 6 Feb 2026 (ending legacy Free) and became the only self-serve plan once legacy Basic and Pro were auto-migrated after 1 Jun and 1 Sep 2026; Composio also removed its managed Twitter credentials in February 2026, so you bring and fund your own app. The real gates are cost and policy: replies only where the account was summoned, no likes, follows or quote-posts on self-serve, and prior approval for AI-generated replies.
drivers: No free tier: prepaid credits and per-request billing for every connected user's calls
No Composio-managed X app since Feb 2026: you must bring your own Client ID, Client Secret and Bearer Token
Self-serve policy limits: summoned-only replies, no likes, follows or quote-posts, prior approval for AI-generated replies
Single-use rotating refresh tokens, plus console and billing glitches that forum users keep reporting
A 3M post reads per month cap before you need Enterprise
summary.bestCase: About an hour to a first working connection (budget at least 4 hours once you add spend limits, tool tests and the confirm-before-post step): sign up at console.x.com, create the app, paste Composio's redirect URI, buy a few dollars of credits (new accounts can get up to $70 free), and connect your account. You never wait on X.
summary.worstCase: Three ways this goes badly. (1) Your X account is flagged, can't create a developer account, and has no working support route. (2) Your AI reply or DM feature needs X's formal written approval, and the only route X staff name is the Enterprise API interest form (which asks you to acknowledge Enterprise pricing), with no pay-per-use channel and no known timeline. (3) You outgrow 3M post reads a month, or need likes, follows or analytics, and must negotiate Enterprise, reportedly starting around $42,000-$50,000 a month.

paths.name: Pay-per-use app with OAuth 2.0 user context
paths.summary: Self-serve X developer account and app on the pay-per-use plan. Users connect through your Composio auth config with OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE. There is no review, but every API call is billed to your prepaid credits.
paths.whenYouNeedIt: Any agent that reads a user's posts, mentions, bookmarks or lists, searches public posts, or publishes posts and replies the user confirms. Since legacy Basic and Pro were migrated to pay-per-use (after 1 Jun and 1 Sep 2026), this is the only self-serve option.

handsOnEffortHours.label: 4-10 hours
handsOnEffortHours.basis: Summed from this path's own steps, setup through live: about 2.5-3.5 h of developer console, billing, test and privacy-policy steps, plus about 4-7 h of agent-preparable work (per-tool cost model, tool tests with charge reconciliation, the confirm-before-post preview X's Developer Policy requires, and limiting tools to what self-serve allows). Getting Access itself lists only three console steps. Allow extra time if you hit console bugs that forum users report (client-not-enrolled, token-generation errors).

evidence.note: Our estimate, summed from this path's step durations. Getting Access: 'Get started with the X API in three steps: sign up, create an app, and save your credentials.' No source gives an hour figure.

approvalWaitDays.label: No review
approvalWaitDays.basis: Neither the Getting Access guide nor the pricing docs include a review or approval step, and keys are generated when you create the app. The exception is an X account flagged by X Support, which cannot sign up at all.

evidence.note: Getting Access: 'The console will generate your API keys and tokens.'

paths.endState: Any X user can authorize your app (your app name appears on X's consent screen), and your agent calls X API v2 on their behalf. Each request is billed to your credit balance, within the 3M post reads per month cap.

stages.name: Create the developer account and app
stages.access: Nobody yet. No OAuth 2.0 client exists, so the only usable tokens are the app owner's own.

steps.title: Pick the X account that will own the app
steps.detail: Use an organization-controlled X account in good standing, with a verified phone number (required to buy credits) and 2FA. Accounts flagged by X Support cannot create developer accounts. Billing and the app are tied to this account, and credits cannot be moved to another account. Apps can't be moved between developer accounts either: X staff say a replacement app gets a new Client ID, so every user would have to re-authorize.

evidence.note: PPU Agreement: 'A verified phone number is required to purchase Credits.'

steps.title: Sign up at console.x.com and accept the agreements
steps.detail: Sign in with that account. Accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, then complete the profile that describes how you will use the API. The PPU Agreement applies when you buy credits. Paste the use-case text from the artifacts.
steps.agentAssist: Drafts the use-case and app description text (artifact 'Use-case and app description').

evidence.note: Getting Access: 'Review and accept the Developer Agreement and Policy.'

steps.title: Create the app inside your Pay-Per-Use project
steps.detail: Click New App, then enter a name, description and use case. Users see the app name on the consent screen, and it is the source label on posts. Keep the app inside the Pay-Per-Use project, not as a standalone app. A standalone app gets 403 client-not-enrolled on every v2 call. If an app ended up standalone, X staff point to Manage apps > Move to package in the console.
steps.agentAssist: Checks the name and description against the use-case text.

evidence.note: Getting Access documents creating the app ('From the Developer Console dashboard, create a new app.'). The project requirement and the 403 come from forum reports and an X staff fix: 'Your app was still Standalone and needed to be moved under Pay-per-use.'

steps.title: Save the API Key/Secret and Bearer Token
steps.detail: Credentials appear only once, and regenerating them invalidates the old ones. Composio's Twitter auth config needs the Bearer Token as well as the OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Secret, so store all of them in your vault.

evidence.note: Getting Access: 'Save immediately. Credentials are only displayed once.'

stages.name: Configure OAuth 2.0 and the Composio auth config
stages.access: Any X user can authorize once the client exists. X has no test-user list, development mode or unverified-app screen. API calls fail until you buy credits.

steps.title: Start a Twitter auth config in Composio and copy its redirect URI
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard, go to Auth Configs, click Create Auth Config, choose Twitter, and switch on the option to use your own developer credentials. Copy the redirect URI the dashboard shows; don't type it from memory. Composio's Twitter guide shows https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but your dashboard's value is the one that counts.
steps.agentAssist: Reads the redirect URI back to you and diffs it against what you paste into X.

evidence.note: Composio: 'For OAuth toolkits, the dashboard shows the redirect URI to add in the provider's developer portal.'

steps.title: Enable OAuth 2.0 in User authentication settings
steps.detail: Open the app, then User authentication settings. App permissions: Read and write (add Direct message only if the agent handles DMs). Type of App: Web App, Automated App or Bot, a confidential client that comes with a Client Secret. Callback URI: paste the Composio redirect URI exactly. Website URL: your product site. Also fill in the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs.
steps.agentAssist: Pre-fills the values in the checklist and confirms each URL resolves over https.

evidence.note: OAuth 2.0 docs: 'Native App and Single page Apps are public clients and Web App and Automated App or bots are confidential clients.'

steps.title: Paste Client ID, Client Secret and Bearer Token into Composio
steps.detail: Finish the auth config with the three credentials. Keep offline.access in the scope list, because without it X issues no refresh token and connections die after 2 hours. Remove scopes your tools don't use, create the config, and store its ac_ ID in your secret manager.
steps.agentAssist: Proposes the minimal scope list for the tools you expose.

evidence.note: Composio guide: 'Fill in with the Client ID, Client Secret from the last step, and the Bearer token from the first step.'

steps.title: Verify endpoints and redirect match
steps.detail: Check that the authorize URL Composio generates uses https://x.com/i/oauth2/authorize, that the token URL is https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token, and that redirect_uri is byte-identical to the registered callback, trailing slash included.
steps.agentAssist: Runs the metadata probe against api.x.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server and compares.

evidence.note: Probe p1 returned authorization_endpoint https://x.com/i/oauth2/authorize and token_endpoint https://api.x.com/2/oauth2/token.

stages.name: Fund the account and set guardrails
stages.access: Any X user can connect. Every call your agent makes for them is charged to your prepaid balance.

steps.title: Add a card and buy credits
steps.detail: Go to Developer Console > Billing. There is no subscription and no minimum spend, and requests are blocked once the balance reaches zero. Accounts paying for the first time can get $20 free after their first purchase on their first eligible card, plus a match of the first auto-recharge up to $50. These incentives are still rolling out, and the free credits expire after 3 months.

evidence.note: Free credits page: 'Free credits from these incentives expire 3 months after they are granted.' Pricing: 'No contracts, subscriptions, or minimum spend.'

steps.title: Set a spending limit and size auto-recharge
steps.detail: Set a spending limit per billing cycle. If you turn on auto-recharge, make each recharge large enough to cover 5 minutes of peak usage. X tops up at most once per 5-minute window and pauses auto-recharge when the balance is zero or negative.
steps.agentAssist: Estimates peak 5-minute spend from expected users and tool calls.

evidence.note: Pricing: 'One top-up per 5-minute window.'

steps.title: Model the per-user cost of each tool
steps.detail: Price each tool the agent has. Self-serve rates: post $0.015, post containing a URL $0.20, summoned reply $0.010, post read $0.005 per post returned, user profile read $0.010, DM event read $0.010, DM send $0.015. A resource fetched twice in one UTC day is billed once. The $0.001 Owned Reads rate covers only the app owner's own data, not your connected users.
steps.agentAssist: Builds the cost model and alert thresholds from your usage assumptions.

evidence.note: Pricing table: Post: Create (with URL) $0.200 per request; Posts: Read $0.005 per resource.

stages.name: Test with your own account
stages.access: You and any teammates you connect. They see the same consent screen production users will see.

steps.title: Connect your own X account through Composio
steps.detail: Start a connection with the auth config, approve it on x.com, and check that the granted scopes include offline.access and tweet.write. X expires the authorization code 30 seconds after the redirect; Composio does the exchange automatically.
steps.agentAssist: Generates the connection link and checks the scopes that come back.

evidence.note: OAuth 2.0 docs: 'You will have to exchange it with an access token within 30 seconds, or the auth_code will expire.'

steps.title: Exercise each tool and reconcile charges
steps.detail: Run every tool you expose (read mentions, search, post, delete) and watch charges per endpoint in the console usage view or via GET /2/usage/tweets. A 402 points to billing. A 403 on posting usually means the token is read-only or the action breaks self-serve rules.
steps.agentAssist: Runs the test script and matches calls to charges.

evidence.note: X staff: 'Regenerate the user token after setting Read and Write, and use that same token for POST /2/tweets.'

steps.title: Confirm refresh after 2 hours
steps.detail: Leave the connection idle for more than 2 hours, then call a tool. Composio should refresh using the stored refresh token. If the connection shows EXPIRED, check that offline.access was granted and that nothing else used the same refresh token.
steps.agentAssist: Schedules the delayed call and reports the result.

evidence.note: OAuth 2.0 docs: access token 'will only stay valid for two hours unless you've used the offline.access scope'.

steps.title: Test revocation
steps.detail: Revoke the app at x.com/settings/connected_apps, then check that your product shows a reconnect prompt.

evidence.note: User access token docs: users 'can revoke access by visiting the connected Apps page'.

stages.name: Launch to users
stages.access: Any X user, with no cap and no review. Rate limits apply (POST /2/tweets: 100 per 15 min per user, 10,000 per 24 h per app), as does the 3M post reads per month cap.

steps.title: Preview and confirm every write
steps.detail: X's Developer Policy requires express, informed consent before you act on a user's behalf, and it requires showing exactly what will be published. Add a confirm step to the agent for every post, reply and DM, and log it.
steps.agentAssist: Implements the confirm-before-send UI and the consent log.

evidence.note: Developer Policy: 'Show exactly what will be published'.

steps.title: Limit tools to what self-serve allows
steps.detail: Only reply when the original author @mentioned or quoted the connected account; X rejects other replies on self-serve, and it also limits programmatic @mentions and quotes in ordinary posts to people already in the conversation. Don't expose like, follow or quote-post write tools, which X removed from self-serve on 20 Apr 2026 (reading likes and follows still works). Composio's Twitter toolkit still lists TWITTER_USER_LIKE_POST, TWITTER_UNLIKE_POST, TWITTER_FOLLOW_USER and TWITTER_UNFOLLOW_USER, so disable them in the auth config or guard them in your agent.
steps.agentAssist: Adds the summoned-reply check and removes the dead tools.

evidence.note: Announcement: 'Following, Likes, and Quote-Posts via API Writes will be removed for all self-serve tiers.' Effective 20 Apr 2026.

steps.title: Publish your privacy policy before users connect
steps.detail: Show the policy before sign-up. It must say what you collect, how you use and share it (including with X), and how people can contact you.
steps.agentAssist: Drafts the X section of the policy (artifact 'Privacy policy outline').

evidence.note: Developer Policy: 'You must display your service’s privacy policy to people before they are permitted to download, install, or sign up to your service.'

steps.title: Monitor balance, spend and the read cap
steps.detail: Alert on low balance, spend approaching the cycle limit, and post reads approaching 3M. Poll GET /2/usage/tweets daily.
steps.agentAssist: Runs the usage poll and posts alerts.

evidence.note: Pricing: 'Monitor your credit balance regularly to avoid service interruptions.'

steps.title: Follow the changelog
steps.detail: X changed prices and self-serve capabilities several times in 2026. Pay-per-use launched Feb 6, the summoned-reply rule arrived Feb 23, Owned Reads and URL-post pricing changed Apr 20, and legacy Basic and Pro were retired after Jun 1 and Sep 1. Subscribe to the changelog RSS.
steps.agentAssist: Watches the RSS feed and flags changes that affect your tools.

evidence.note: Changelog entries dated 2026-02-06, 2026-02-23 and 2026-04-16; forum announcements for the Basic and Pro migrations.

steps.title: Plan for re-authorization
steps.detail: Changing app permissions means users must re-authorize to get tokens with the new scope. X staff say rotating the client secret does not invalidate existing user tokens, but every later code exchange and refresh must use the new secret, so update the Composio auth config the moment you rotate. A replacement app does force every user to reconnect, because it gets a new Client ID. Build a reconnect flow.
steps.agentAssist: Builds the reconnect prompt and a rotation runbook.

evidence.note: Apps docs: 'Changing permissions requires users to re-authorize your app to get new tokens with the updated scope.' X staff (2026-08-14): 'Existing user access tokens and refresh tokens stay valid.'

paths.name: AI-generated replies or DMs (prior written approval from X)
paths.summary: The same pay-per-use app, plus X's prior written approval before you deploy AI-generated replies. The developer forum gives only informal rulings (staff say a mention-only design 'appears to align' with the rules, which is not written approval). On 14 Oct 2026 X staff said formal written approval goes through the Enterprise API interest form, even for pay-per-use apps, and that there is no other channel. There is no SLA, and no one has reported an outcome from that route.
paths.whenYouNeedIt: The agent itself writes and sends replies to mentions, or answers DMs, on a connected account. Human-confirmed sends are contested: on 17 Aug 2026 X staff said AI replies need approval even with a human click before send, but on 27 Aug staff said human-reviewed drafts sent only after an explicit Send click (inbound only, one reply per interaction) need no additional written approval. X staff say AI-drafted original posts that a human approves do not need this, but automated posting still needs the Automated label.

handsOnEffortHours.basis: Build and document opt-in triggers, one reply per interaction, opt-out handling and automated labels, then write and follow up on the request. Our estimate, based on the safeguards X staff list in approval threads.

Since 13 Oct staff say the forum issues no written approvals. At least three approval threads (6 and 13 May, 1 Aug 2026) auto-closed after 14 days with no staff reply. Formal written approval now goes through the Enterprise API interest form, and no timeline or outcome has been reported for it. The 90-day max mirrors this guide's Enterprise sales estimate; it is a planning placeholder, not an observed figure.

composio.note: Composio removed its managed Twitter credentials in February 2026, so every Twitter integration needs your own X app. Create a custom auth config with your Client ID, Client Secret and Bearer Token, and register the redirect URI the Composio dashboard shows. X bills your developer account for every call Composio makes for your users, so cost grows with usage. If you also make X API calls yourself, don't refresh the same tokens outside Composio.

evidence.note: Composio: 'As of February 2026, Composio managed credentials for the Twitter toolkit have been removed.'

oauth.refreshTokens: Issued only if the authorization requested offline.access. Refresh with POST /2/oauth2/token grant_type=refresh_token (confidential clients authenticate with HTTP Basic client_id:client_secret; the metadata lists only 'none' and 'client_secret_basic'). Refresh tokens are single-use: X's OAuth 1.0a token-exchange guide says each refresh returns a new one (X DevRel said the same on the forum in 2022), so the refresh token you just sent stops working. X keeps one live grant per app and user, so authorizing the same app from a second client revokes the first client's tokens. Tokens are invalidated when the user revokes at x.com/settings/connected_apps. X staff say rotating the client secret does not invalidate them, though later refreshes must use the new secret. Revoke from the app side with POST /2/oauth2/revoke. Since 21 Sep 2026, OAuth 1.0a user tokens can be exchanged for OAuth 2.0 tokens with the token-exchange grant.
oauth.tokenLifetime: Access token: 2 hours (expires_in 7200). Authorization code: must be exchanged within 30 seconds. Refresh token: about 6 months, per X's OAuth 1.0a token-exchange guide (which says exchanged tokens behave like ordinary OAuth 2.0 tokens) and a 2022 X DevRel forum reply. The main OAuth 2.0 pages don't state it.
oauth.redirectUris: Exact match, including protocol and trailing slash. Up to 10 callback URLs per app. Use https in production. For local development the Apps doc says to use http://127.0.0.1, not localhost (though X's own Ads MCP page registers http://localhost:8080/callback for some clients). javascript:, data:, file: and other non-standard schemes are rejected. A mismatch gives 'Callback URL not approved for this client application.' (code 415). Register exactly the URI your Composio auth config shows.
oauth.scopes: Fine-grained, space-separated scopes chosen at authorization, for example tweet.read, users.read, tweet.write, media.write, dm.read, dm.write, bookmark.read, list.read, users.email and offline.access. The consent screen lists them. X documents the App permissions setting (Read / Read and write / Read, write and Direct message) as an OAuth 1.0a control, but X staff blame OAuth 2.0 posting 403s on tokens that are 'still read-only', so set Read and write before users connect and have users reconnect if you change it. like.write and follows.write still exist in the docs, but the endpoints were removed from self-serve on 20 Apr 2026. The live metadata scopes_supported list is incomplete (it omits tweet.write, and its grant_types_supported omits the token-exchange grant), so don't rely on it.

evidence.note: Probe p1 (re-run 2026-10-20): S256 only, grant types authorization_code and refresh_token, no registration_endpoint. Docs: 2-hour access tokens, refresh token only with offline.access, exact-match callbacks; token-exchange guide: refresh token 'valid for about 6 months and single-use'.

nuances.title: Replies only where the account was summoned

nuances.title: Refresh tokens are single-use
nuances.detail: Each refresh returns a new refresh token and invalidates the old one. If you must refresh yourself, use a single-flight lock and save the new pair before using it.

nuances.title: Sharing credentials with Composio vs. X's security clause
nuances.detail: The PPU Agreement says you 'will not make available to any third party any token, key, password, or other login credentials to the X API'. Composio holds your client secret and users' tokens on your behalf, and X has published no guidance on integration platforms. nuances.title: Free access is only for public-utility apps
nuances.detail: Since 6 Feb 2026, only apps X classifies as Public Utility Apps keep free scaled access. A commercial AI agent should not count on it.

evidence.note: Launch post: 'only apps classified as Public Utility Apps will continue to receive free scaled access.'

nuances.title: One live grant per app and user
nuances.detail: X keeps a single live OAuth grant per (app, user): when a user authorizes the same X app from a second client, X revokes the first client's tokens. If you point another integration at the same X app (your own OAuth code, an MCP client, a second Composio auth config), the user's Composio connection stops working. A user reconnecting through the same auth config probably replaces the older grant the same way. Use one X app per client.

blockers.symptom: Every v2 call returns 403 Client Forbidden with reason client-not-enrolled. The console may say 'This client app has already been added to your project.'
blockers.cause: The app is standalone or stuck in a ghost project, usually after a legacy-plan migration.

evidence.note: Forum: 403 'client-not-enrolled'; Composio FAQ: 'Verify the app is linked to a project'.

blockers.title: POST /2/tweets returns 403 'not permitted'
blockers.symptom: Posting fails with 403 'You are not permitted to perform this action', even though tweet.write was granted and media upload works.
blockers.cause: Possible causes: the user's token was minted while App permissions were Read only; the reply wasn't summoned; or an account-level posting or integrity limit.
blockers.resolution: Set App permissions to Read and write, have the user reconnect so a new token is minted, reply only in summoned conversations, and check whether the account can post on x.com itself.

evidence.note: Staff: 'Regenerate the user token after setting Read and Write'.

blockers.title: Callback URL not approved

blockers.title: Connections go EXPIRED

evidence.note: OAuth docs: 'If this scope is not passed, we will not generate a refresh token.'

<YOUR_APP_NAME> connects your X account to your AI assistant. It can read your posts, mentions, bookmarks and lists, and it drafts posts and replies that you review and approve before anything is published.

Whether the Enterprise API interest form, which X staff named on 14 Oct 2026 as the only route for formal written approval of AI-powered replies (including for pay-per-use apps), actually produces a written approval without an Enterprise contract, and how long it takes. Enterprise pricing and time to contract are not published. The $42k-$50k/month figures come from two forum users describing the interest form; the form itself is a help.x.com iframe that blocks automated fetches, so the budget bands weren't confirmed.
The minimum one-time credit purchase amount, and whether the console demands a purchase before you can create an app.
Whether the PKCE 'plain' method still works. The docs say S256 or plain; the live metadata advertises only S256.
Whether console.x.com signup asks for a specific use-case form or character limits. It couldn't be inspected without logging in.

Which POST /2/tweets per-user limit applies: the rate-limits table says 100 per 15 min (10,000 per 24 h per app), while the Manage Posts integration guide says 200 per 15 min plus 300 posts and reposts per 3 hours.
Whether X's single live grant per (app, user) rule, documented on the Ads MCP page, also revokes an earlier Composio connection when the same user connects twice through one auth config.

Whether human-confirmed AI replies (the user clicks Send on each one) need X's prior written approval. Staff said yes on 17 Aug 2026 and, for inbound-only, one-per-interaction replies, no on 27 Aug 2026.

verification.summary: Checked 31 high-impact claims: 20 supported, 8 corrected, 1 downgraded, 2 unverifiable. The biggest correction: since 14 Oct 2026, X staff route formal written approval for AI-generated replies through the Enterprise API interest form rather than the forum, even for pay-per-use apps, so that path is now Gated. Also, X's token-exchange guide does document the 6-month, single-use refresh token. A cross-guide calibration pass on 2026-10-20 raised the recommended path's effort to 4-10 hours so it covers the path's own step durations, and aligned two wait labels with their numbers (v32-v33).

Endpoints, S256, auth methods and the missing registration_endpoint are unchanged; OIDC discovery still 404; token endpoint still returns 400 invalid_client 'Value passed for the client id was invalid.'

entries.claim: Access token lasts 2 hours, refresh token only with offline.access, auth code must be exchanged within 30 seconds

entries.claim: Refresh-token lifetime of about 6 months is only in a 2022 forum reply, not in current docs
entries.before: Refresh token: about 6 months, per a 2022 X DevRel forum reply; not in current docs.
entries.after: About 6 months per X's OAuth 1.0a token-exchange guide (2026) and the 2022 DevRel reply; the main OAuth 2.0 pages don't state it.
entries.note: The token-exchange guide says the returned refresh token is 'valid for about 6 months' and that exchanged tokens are 'ordinary OAuth 2.0 user tokens with the same refresh flow'. The open question was narrowed to whether the 6 months restart on each refresh.

entries.before: n6 evidence reported/medium, 'Not stated in current docs.'
entries.after: n6 evidence documented/high, citing the token-exchange guide; oauth.refreshTokens cites it too.
entries.note: Token-exchange guide: refresh token is 'single-use; each refresh returns a new one.' The 2022 DevRel statement and the OpenTweet blog agree.

entries.note: Staff (14 Aug 2026): 'Existing user access tokens and refresh tokens stay valid' and 'You can’t transfer an app between developer accounts. A new app gets a new Client ID'.

entries.after: The Apps doc says to use http://127.0.0.1, not localhost, though X's own Ads MCP page registers http://localhost:8080/callback for some clients.

entries.claim: AI-generated replies need X's prior approval, and staff say this holds even with a human click before send

entries.note: Found by searching for forum threads after 13 Oct 2026. b4, b7, art3, agentVsYou and openQuestions were updated.

entries.before: 0-14 days, 'Same day to no answer (no SLA)'; 'those were rulings ... not written approvals'; one request (1 Aug 2026) auto-closed.

entries.note: A second forum user (14 Oct 2026) reports the same $50,000/month acknowledgment, so c2 and r12 now cite both. The form is a help.x.com iframe that returned 403 to curl, so the figures weren't confirmed at source. Kept as reported/low.

entries.note: PPU Agreement: 'A verified phone number is required to purchase Credits', section VII.F (non-transferable), clause (k) 'fine-tune or train a foundation or frontier model', clause G (Security). Guidelines: 'App stores X data to train AI/ML models' is 'Prohibited (except Grok)'.

entries.note: Developer Policy quotes appear verbatim ('does not by itself constitute consent', 'Show exactly what will be published', 'You must display your service’s privacy policy ... before they are permitted to ... sign up').

entries.note: Neither the Apps page nor Composio's guide lists the form fields, and the console is a logged-in client-rendered app. The guide already says this couldn't be checked; the advice to fill them in stands.

entries.note: The forum thread has the error body, the staff fix ('Your app was still Standalone and needed to be moved under Pay-per-use ... Manage apps > Move to package') and the follow-on 402 CreditsDepleted. Composio's FAQ agrees.

entries.note: Staff (14 Aug 2026) quoted verbatim. The Apps page heads permissions 'App permissions (OAuth 1.0a)', so the OAuth 2.0 effect stays reported.

entries.note: Staff (14 Oct 2026): 'Accounts flagged by support are unable to create developer accounts.' The reporter describes the circular Help Center loop.

entries.claim: Difficulty 3 (Moderate) for the recommended pay-per-use path
entries.note: A judgment call. There is no review (that alone would be 1-2), but mandatory prepaid per-call billing for every connected user's calls, with no free tier, plus the policy limits push it up. It falls short of 4 because the entry cost is a few dollars, not a fixed fee or assessment.

entries.claim: Best case: about an hour of setup
entries.after: About an hour to a first working connection (budget 2 or more hours once you add spend limits, tool tests and the confirm-before-post step): ...
